text:
Ava (Support): Hey team, getting a high-sev from a customer using the /rerank endpoint. They see 500s and sometimes a sudden drop to 0 scores when inputs include emoji sequences and some invisible chars (zero-width joiner, BOM-like bytes). Repro included. Reporting customer impact: production traffic ~10 requests/min hitting rerank -> intermittent failures. :warning:

build-bot: ERROR log forwarded from prod (service=rerank, pod=rerank-5a7f):
```
ERROR RuntimeError: Failed to score batch
  at score_batch (/app/runtime/score.py:142)
  caused by UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 12: invalid start byte
  request_id=xyz-123
  payload_summary={"items":7, "avg_tokens":18}
```

Sam (Eng): Can you paste the exact client payload (sanitized) and the customer timestamp so I can grep traces? Also, is the failure deterministic if they resend the same body? :eyes:

Ava (Support): Customer provided this sample body (they said they had to copy/paste, might have hidden chars):
```
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "queries": ["Which restaurant is open late?\u200d\uFE0F"],
  "candidates": ["Joe's Diner\u0000", "24/7 Café\uEF\BB\BF", "Best Eats 😊\x80\x80"]
}
```
They said exact bytes came from a mobile client that does some legacy concatenation + emoji picker. They see: 500s ~1 in 20, and when successful some candidate scores become `0.0` or `NaN`.

Priya (ML): The `NaN`/`0.0` smells like an eval path when any tensor gets an invalid value (e.g., inf/NaN) from text->embed -> similarity. Malformed UTF-8 can create weird tokenization. We should capture the tokenized ids for the failing payload. If tokens are empty or contain unexpected sentinel values the scorer might divide by zero.

Zack (SRE): I pulled the logs around `xyz-123` across pods. There's a downstream decode routine in the HTTP layer that calls `body.decode('utf-8')` without strict handling. When it hits `0x80` it raises and bubbles up as 500. We have a middleware that is supposed to catch `UnicodeDecodeError` and return 400, but it doesn't in the rerank route because the handler does `raw = await req.body(); text = raw.decode()` inside a try but the exception gets swallowed and re-raised later due to a join on a threadpool. Looks like a bug.

Sam (Eng): Repro locally with the exact bytes and confirm. I ran this (node curl to send raw bytes):
```
echo -n '{"queries":["a\u200d\uFE0F"],"candidates":["foo\u0000","bar\x80"]}' | \
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/rerank -d @- -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```
On my end, service returns 500 and stacktrace points to `json.loads(text)` failing because `text` is a Python `str` built from a decode that already substituted replacement chars.

Priya (ML): Two things to consider: (1) Reject malformed/invalid-utf8 with a clear 400 + error code so clients can fix; (2) Optional: run unicode normalization (NFC) and strip zero-width/BOM characters, but that can change semantic matching and will affect rerank scores — we must surface that change to customers.

Ava (Support): Customer (Elijah) chimed in: "We get a batch of user-supplied titles from mobile. We can't easily sanitize on client because some users copy/paste from other apps. We need either the API to handle it gracefully or a clear error we can act on."

Elijah (Customer): Confirming — we've started receiving 500s in prod at 2028-06-15T14:23:10Z. If the API can return a deterministic 400 with a message like `invalid-encoding: candidate[1] contains invalid byte 0x80`, we'd accept that and build a client-side sanitizer.

Sam (Eng): Plan proposal: quick patch to the rerank HTTP handler to: 
1) Use `raw = await req.body()` then attempt `text = raw.decode('utf-8', errors='strict')` inside a top-level try.
2) If `UnicodeDecodeError`, return 400 with JSON error containing `invalid_encoding` and the offending byte position (no PII).
3) Instrument metrics for `rerank.invalid_encoding` and add a sampling of raw bytes to S3 with redaction for engineering triage.
Estimated deploy: hotfix to staging in 2 hrs, prod in next deploy window + rollback on failure.

Priya (ML): Acceptable. Add a toggle to enable optional `unicode_normalize=true` on requests so customers can ask for server-side normalization. But default must be conservative (reject) to avoid silent score shifts. We'll add a warning in docs.

Zack (SRE): Also adding a middleware test to our integration suite to send these byte sequences to ensure future regressions don't slip. I'll create an incident ticket to track and mark P1 until hotfix is in prod.

Sam (Eng): I reproduced tokenization diff: when we run tokenizer on sanitized NFC text vs raw bytes, token IDs differ for emoji+zwj sequences which changes ranking weights. See sample snippet: 
```
raw bytes -> tokenizer ids: [101, 4012, 0, 502]
sanitized NFC -> tokenizer ids: [101, 4012, 502]
```
So normalization will change score ordering in edge cases. We'll document it.

Ava (Support): I'll reply to Elijah with the mitigation plan: (1) We'll rollout a validation that returns 400 for invalid bytes; (2) Offer a `unicode_normalize` flag in next release; (3) Ask them to optionally sanitize client-side for immediate relief. Marking this thread for follow-up after prod deploy. :white_check_mark:

Elijah (Customer): Thanks, that works for us. Please keep me posted on the deploy window and any request schema changes so we can update our clients.

Sam (Eng): Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank/compare/fix/utf8-validate (draft) — adds strict decode + test cases for NUL, ZWJ, BOM, and lone continuation bytes. Will add metric and SLO check.

Ava (Support): Setting follow-up reminder in 24h. Assigning to Sam to shepherd the patch. Thanks all. :pray:
